article.title: Coking coal and iron ore surge after cyclone shuts Queensland export terminals
article.text: Seaborne coking coal and iron ore prices surged after a cyclone shut two Queensland export terminals and disrupted rail haulage from the Bowen Basin, with loadings not expected to normalise for several weeks. Mills that buy imported coking coal face an immediate cost step-up, and long-steel prices in India have already been marked higher on the domestic trade. Cost consultants noted that a sustained higher steel price feeds through, with a lag, into the project cost base of the entire construction and infrastructure order book -- an economy-wide input into award economics rather than a development at any one contractor.
article.note: Blueprint §32 scenario 11, SECOND observation of the MACRO_CONTEXT tier on a deliberately different chain, event type and directness verdict from inr_it_multihop_macro_context. Here the multi-hop runs coking coal / iron ore (d1) -> domestic steel price pass-through (d2) -> infrastructure project cost inflation (d3), on `commodity_price` -- the other broad event type no archetype claims -- so the dynamic ripple path is what reaches d3, exactly as in the INR fixture but through unrelated machinery. Directness lands REMOTE here (a novel node the registry does not own, so the d3 distance fallback applies) where the INR fixture lands DIRECT (a registry mechanism rated DIRECT sitting three hops out); the two together pin §11 from BOTH sides: directness is decided independently of tier AND of distance.

ground_truth.rationale: A SECOND, structurally independent observation of the macro-context tier, so the metric does not ride on one file. Coking coal -> domestic steel price -> infrastructure project cost is a genuine three-hop chain and a genuine claim, but it is a claim about the cost base of an entire order book across an industry, which §7 says must be presented as context rather than dressed up as a company-specific verdict. LT clears the d3 causal-path bar the only way it can be cleared -- relationship-grade evidence (a CURATED, independently sourced order-book sensitivity record = tier C) plus a HIGH composite materiality grade -- and lands at MACRO_CONTEXT, structurally unable to reach primary or secondary_ripple, both of which close above d2. NCC sits at the same node with the same distance, the same direction and a verifier accept, backed by nothing but the model's own inference (tier E, materiality capped LOW), so the causal-path gate rejects it as REJECT_LOW_PRIORITY. Deliberately different from inr_it_multihop_macro_context in event type (commodity_price, not macro_data), in chain, in effect sign, and in DIRECTNESS: this row is REMOTE (a novel node the registry does not own, so the distance fallback decides) where the INR row is DIRECT (a registry mechanism rated DIRECT that happens to sit three hops from its event). One tier, two directness verdicts -- §11 holds from both sides.
ground_truth.universe_note: The universe deliberately carries only the d3 slice (the two contractors). The steel producers at d1/d2 are real and would be real candidates in production; including them here would add a second, unrelated tier decision to a fixture whose whole subject is what happens at the THIRD hop. The two contractors DO ride the candidate pool at the d1 and d2 nodes as well, so those mapping calls carry an EXPLICIT empty response rather than relying on the harness default -- the fixture states that the model correctly declines to call a contractor a casualty of the coal price or of the mill's own repricing, and names it only where the chain actually reaches its cost base.
